claims.text: CoCrFeMnNi-based HEA multilayers can be used to probe and control a transition between diffusion-dominated and dislocation-mediated creep.
Changing layer thickness can tune interface coherency in CoCrFeMnNi-based HEA multilayers.
Changing interface composition can tune interface coherency in CoCrFeMnNi-based HEA multilayers.
CoCrFeMnNi can form a single-phase alloy.
The proposed CoCrFeMnNi-based multilayers can be fully dense.
The proposed multilayers can initially have uniform interfaces and minimal defect density.
Increasing interface mismatch produces misfit-dislocation networks at the HEA layer interfaces.
Interfacial misfit-dislocation networks alter the dominant creep mechanism as temperature or stress increases.
Highly coherent interfaces cause creep to be predominantly limited by diffusion across interface boundaries.
Accumulated misfit strain and loss of coherency cause dislocation-mediated deformation to increasingly govern creep.
A threshold interface mismatch or layer thickness separates diffusion-controlled creep from dislocation-driven creep.
Crossing the proposed threshold produces a transition from slower diffusion-controlled creep to faster dislocation-driven creep.
Highly coherent CoCrFeMnNi-based HEA multilayers exhibit diffusion-dominated creep at moderate service temperatures.
Second-phase precipitation or large-scale defects may shift the proposed creep-mechanism transition.
Behavior above about 700 °C may depart from the proposed transition regime.
